data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The 3-of-26 result is a confound of registry size: a test constrains its subject only when the registry of expected failures is small enough that each mutation is a decision, and the 1/9 vs 4/4 to 6/7 spread is the ratio of mutations to registry entries in each module, not a property of the tests themselves.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the registry is rebuilt from scratch for each mutation, registry size is irrelevant.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 3-of-26 survivors are in modules with small registries, this explanation fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the mutation testing framework uses a fixed threshold for 'caught' rather than a registry, this mechanism does not apply.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the author manually reviewed every mutation result, registry size cannot explain the distribution.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The mutation testing framework works by maintaining a registry of expected failures. When the registry is small, each mutation is a decision: is this the new passing state or is the test wrong? When the registry is large, mutations are absorbed into the noise. The 3-of-26 survivors are the mutations that landed in modules where the registry was large enough to absorb them. The 1/9 lost mutation in compile.py is the one case where the registry was small enough that the mutation was a decision, but the decision was made in the wrong direction.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
